CDP vs LLDP: who made each, and which is on by default on Cisco gear?

CDP: Cisco proprietary, on by default.
LLDP: IEEE 802.1AB standard, off by default on Cisco.
How do you turn on LLDP on a Cisco device?
lldp run in global config. Check with show lldp neighbors.
A Cisco router connects to a Juniper switch, and show cdp neighbors is empty. Why, and what do you do?
Juniper doesn't speak CDP. Turn on LLDP with lldp run; Juniper speaks LLDP.
On R1, show cdp neighbors: Device ID SW1, Local Intrfce Gig 0/0, Port ID Gig 0/1. Which SW1 port is R1 plugged into?
Gi0/1. Port ID is the neighbor's port; Local Intrfce is your own.
On SW1, show cdp neighbors: Device ID R1, Local Intrfce Gig 1/0/24, Port ID Gig 0/0/1. Which port on each device is the link?
SW1's Gi1/0/24 (Local Intrfce) connects to R1's Gi0/0/1 (Port ID).
show cdp neighbors doesn't show the neighbor's IP. How do you get it?
show cdp neighbors detail
Does CDP need IP configured to work?
No. It's Layer 2, sent directly on the link.
Can CDP show a device two switches away? Can ARP?

CDP: no, only directly connected neighbors.
ARP: yes, if it's on the same subnet and has talked, but ARP can't tell how far away it is.
You just ran lldp run and show lldp neighbors is empty. Problem?
Probably not yet. LLDP advertises every 30 seconds by default; wait for the next one.
What are the default CDP and LLDP timers?

CDP: advertise every 60 s, hold 180 s.
LLDP: advertise every 30 s, hold 120 s.
CDP and LLDP are both off. How do you find which switch port a router's Gi0/0 is plugged into?
Get Gi0/0's MAC from show interfaces on the router, then find that MAC in the switch's table with show mac address-table.
Why turn CDP off on an ISP-facing interface, and how?
It advertises your device name, model, IOS version, and IP to whoever's on the other end. no cdp enable on that interface (no cdp run turns it off everywhere).
